I still remember the challenge we faced with data quality in our analytics pipeline. We had a large-scale ETL process handling 500M+ daily records, and ensuring data accuracy was a top priority. 

The problem was that our traditional testing approach was time-consuming and often caught errors too late in the process. That's when we decided to leverage dbt tests and data contracts to enforce data quality at the model layer. 

We started by defining clear data contracts using dbt's `schema.yml` file, specifying the expected structure and constraints for each model. Then, we wrote targeted tests using `dbt test` commands to validate data against these contracts. 

The result was a significant reduction in data errors and a 40% decrease in ETL runtime. By shifting left and testing data at the model layer, we were able to catch issues earlier and improve overall data quality. 

Our reusable ETL framework, built using dbt, Docker, and GitHub Actions CI/CD, further accelerated our deployment cycle by 35%. It was a game-changer for our team, and I'm excited to apply similar approaches in my next role.
